answer: The opal test I would run is Proof of unique courier account with delivery history: parcels sent and signed for over three years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so parcels sent and signed for over three years stays private; the bridge is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the cipher of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
